q: Which material is the core constituent of conventional gypsum board?
n: Gypsum board uses a gypsum core faced with paper or other facings depending on product type.

q: Why is a waste allowance normally added after a pure-area tile count?
o: Cuts, breakage and spares add to it
n: Area division gives only the theoretical minimum; actual orders include waste and cutting allowance.
Natural gypsum is calcium sulfate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O.

q: If one coat covers 25 m² per gallon, what area can two gallons cover for one coat?
What two geometric floor qualities are commonly quantified separately in F-number systems?
n: F-number systems distinguish local surface flatness from longer-wavelength levelness.

q: Why is cornice length usually based on the full room perimeter rather than deducting door openings?
o: It runs above the door openings too
Doors are ignored in all estimates
ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated
n: A room cornice follows the ceiling perimeter continuously unless specifically interrupted.

q: Which use typically demands exceptionally high floor flatness and levelness because vehicles or systems are sensitive to small deviations?
o: Warehouse floors used by air-pallet systems
ref: ACI 117 / ASTM E1155 floor flatness and levelness concepts
n: Special material-handling systems such as air pallets require exceptionally flat floors compared with ordinary finishes.

q: A 3.60 m × 3.20 m room receives 0.40 m square tiles. How many tiles are required by area before waste?
Why must a walkable/interstitial ceiling have greater structural capacity than an ordinary suspended ceiling?
o: It must carry workers and services
ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated
n: Personnel access adds live-load demands beyond those of a purely suspended finish ceiling.

q: Why is a baseboard typically interrupted at a door opening?
o: There is no wall at the door opening
ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated
n: Baseboard follows the wall-foot perimeter and is normally omitted across the clear doorway.

q: How many 0.40 m × 0.40 m tiles are required by pure area calculation, rounding up to whole pieces?
ref: TCNA Handbook; calculated from the stated situation givens
n: The room area is 14.28 m² and each tile covers 0.16 m²; 14.28/0.16=89.25, so 90 whole tiles are required before waste.

q: If 25 m² per gallon is interpreted as coverage per coat, how many whole gallons are required for three coats on the walls and ceiling?
ref: Architectural coating quantity estimating; calculated from stated situation givens
n: Using the explicit per-coat interpretation, the net wall plus ceiling area is about 50.83 m². Three coats require 152.49 m² of coverage; 152.49/25=6.10 gallons, so seven whole gallons are needed.

q: How many 1.20 m × 2.40 m gypsum boards are required by pure area calculation, before waste?
ref: ASTM C1396/C1396M; calculated from stated dimensions
n: The ceiling is 14.28 m² and one board covers 2.88 m²; 14.28/2.88=4.96, which rounds up to five boards.

q: A 17.28 m² ceiling uses 1.20×2.40 m gypsum board. How many full boards are required before waste?
Which tool can check both horizontal level and vertical plumb?
ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction
n: A spirit level with horizontal and vertical vials checks both level and plumb.

q: Approximately how many board feet are required for the room's 1×4 baseboard and 1×3 cornice, using the perimeter lengths and deducting the door only from the baseboard?
ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate
n: Baseboard length is 15.20−0.70=14.50 m and cornice length is the full 15.20 m. Converting to feet and applying the board-foot formula gives about 28.3 bd ft.

q: A classroom has two 3 ft × 7 ft door openings and uses 3 in × 6 in jamb stock ordered in 18 ft lengths. For 10 classrooms, what board-foot quantity corresponds to one 18 ft length per door?
ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate
n: There are 20 doors. One 3×6×18 ft stock length contains 27 board feet, so 20 lengths total 540 board feet.

q: What is an interstitial ceiling in the context of building services?
o: A walkable ceiling for service access
ref: Francis D.K. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated
n: Interstitial ceiling/service zones are intended to support access for service installation and maintenance.
